assessment: The incumbent offers a repeatable conversational routine, printed access and optional messaging. Seven frequent attendees value its structure, and nine participants regularly rely on print. Its usefulness is uneven: five occasional attendees struggle to enter conversations familiar to their partners, a concrete limit on treating repetition as universally helpful. This does not establish why entry is difficult. Of 72 slips, 49 report ten useful minutes and 48 identify the intended preparation task; 97 attendances occurred, so incomplete reporting and untimed speaking prevent a complete outcome estimate. Coordination sometimes exceeds 90 minutes. Pairing delays and partner changes identify possible friction without proving proficiency mismatch.

openings.claim: Unequal familiarity with the conversation may impede occasional attendees even when the repeated session structure helps frequent attendees. A self-contained opening prompt followed by alternating speaker turns may improve entry while retaining that structure.
openings.delta: Separates familiarity with the routine from familiarity with conversation content; neither public proficiency labels nor attendance prerequisites are needed.
openings.prediction: Pairs using the self-contained opening show fewer early restarts or partner changes and more balanced speaking time; usefulness reports improve particularly among participants reporting unfamiliarity with the topic.
openings.probe: Within existing sessions, offer randomly allocated pairs either usual prompts or the self-contained opening, with voluntary switching. Anonymous observation records entry delay and speaking distribution; exit slips ask usefulness and topic familiarity. Keep the 75-minute limit and log volunteer time.
assumptions: Topic familiarity can be reported anonymously without a proficiency label.
Existing volunteers can prepare the small prompt variation within available time.

openings.claim: Confusion between earlier and next preparation tasks may partly reflect unclear temporal identification on otherwise accessible printed material. A dated, consistently positioned next-session box could reduce that confusion.
openings.delta: Tests task-version recognition separately from speaking-practice quality and does not require digital access.
openings.prediction: Compared with usual sheets, dated boxes reduce earlier-task answers; unchanged blank answers would limit the account to temporal confusion.
openings.probe: Alternate usual and dated sheet formats across six sessions, retaining printed availability at arrival and departure. Count correct, earlier and blank preparation answers separately and record total weekly coordination minutes. Attendance differences limit causal attribution.
assumptions: The next task is settled before printing.
Dates and task wording are understandable to participants.
